(v. <cite ref="L00398"><he>לָטַשׁ</he></cite>, a. <cite ref="S00810"><he>קָטַף</he></cite>); <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 14">Gen. senses.gloss: to slap and crush the earth under the olive tree; to hoe.
units: <cite ref="Moed Katan 3a:7">M. Kat. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>יכול לא יְקַשְׁקֵשׁ תחת וכ׳</he> lest you think that one may not hoe under the olive trees &c. (in the Sabbatical year).

<cite ref="Moed Katan 3a:10">Ib.</cite> <he>תשמטנה מלְקַשְׁקֵשׁ וכ׳</he> ‘thou shalt let it rest’ (<cite ref="Exodus 23:11">Ex. XXIII, 11</cite>) from hoeing &c.; <cite ref="Sukkah 44b">Succ. 44ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 354">Yalk. Ex. 354</cite> (corr. acc.); a. e.
<cite ref="Chullin 74b:17">Ḥull. 74ᵇ</cite> <he>כאגוז המִתְקַשְׁקֵשׁ וכ׳</he> like a nut that rattles in its shell.
<cite ref="Chullin 94a:13">Ib. 94ᵃ</cite> <he>לגין המתקשקש</he> a bottle which gives a sound when shaken (half-filled).

<cite ref="Chullin 125a:16">Ib. 125ᵃ</cite> <he>מוח המתק׳</he> brain that shakes in the skull; a. e.—[<cite ref="Niddah 47a:53">Nidd. 47ᵃ</cite> <he>משׁיִתְקַשְׁקְשׁוּ הדדין</he> when the breasts begin to shake (in walking), comment.; v., however, <cite ref="S02258"><he>קִשְׁקֵשׁ</he> II</cite>.]
